svg.title: MarkeTech frontend: the path of a request
svg.desc: Panel A: in development, npm run dev:link starts Vite, which serves the source files and proxies /api and /_allauth to the Django backend, and /ws as a WebSocket; in production the Docker image builds dist and Nginx serves it, answering index.html for every application address, passing /api, /_allauth, /admin and /static to the backend container, and /ws/ with the Upgrade headers. Panel B: the browser loads index.html, then main.ts loads Poppins 400 and 600, creates the Vue application with the i18n and router plugins and mounts App.vue, which lays out the header, the side bar, the RouterView and the footer; the router has 27 routes, and RouterView displays the page matching the address, such as HomePage.vue. Panel C: the frame and the pages call session.ts or the nine domain files of src/api/, which go through api/http.ts, the only file that calls fetch; the requests reach Django through the Vite proxy or Nginx. In real time, live.ts opens one WebSocket to /ws/ per tab while someone is logged in; the server sends signals, and the listeners registered with onNews read again through the API. Panel D: moving between pages does not ask the server for a new page.
svg.text: MarkeTech frontend: the path of a request
From the address typed by the user to the page on screen, from the page to the backend, and back in real time. Follow the numbers 1 to 17.
Real files of the repository as of 30.10.2026 (commit a7f8fb3).
Two servers for the same files
Vite on the workstation · Nginx in Docker, on your PC or in production
in the browser, each time an address is opened or refreshed
in the browser, when a page sends a form, needs data, or hears news
no new page is asked from the server
Start it once, leave it running.

svg.text: production only; absent on your PC
Same rule for both servers, so the code in the browser (panels B and C) never knows which one answers
A file that exists is sent as is. Any other address gets index.html: the application chooses the page.
/api, /_allauth and /ws are not files: they are passed to the backend, /ws as a WebSocket. Each new prefix is added on both sides.

svg.text: The server only says what changed: { type: "messages" | "applications" | "appointments", application: 12 }.
The listener reads again through src/api/ (step 11 again), so the API alone decides what the user
may see. After a cut, and when the tab comes back to the front, every listener hears null: read all again.
Server side of real time (consumer, signals sent by the views): backend/docs/backend-realtime.svg
